title: Speed Up CI With a Matrix and Dependency Caching
intro: Your library supports Node 18, 20, and 22, but CI only tests 20 — and every run spends 90 seconds re-downloading the same dependencies.

steps.starter_content:
name: CI
on: [push, pull_request]
jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm test
steps.prompt: Change the 'test' job to (1) run once per Node version using strategy.matrix.node-version: [18, 20, 22], (2) pass node-version: ${{ matrix.node-version }} to setup-node, and (3) enable npm dependency caching by adding cache: npm to setup-node's 'with' block.
steps.hint: strategy goes directly under jobs.test (same level as runs-on). The matrix value must be a list. Inside steps, ${{ matrix.node-version }} is replaced with each value in turn — one full job run per value.
steps.solution:
name: CI
on: [push, pull_request]
jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      matrix:
        node-version: [18, 20, 22]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: ${{ matrix.node-version }}
          cache: npm
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm test
steps.fake_output:
✓ test (18)  52s   cache hit
✓ test (20)  49s   cache hit
✓ test (22)  51s   cache hit
steps.explanation: Three parallel jobs, one per Node version, each restoring cached dependencies instead of downloading them.
steps.why: The matrix catches 'works on 20, breaks on 18' before your users do, and the three jobs run in parallel, so it costs no extra wall-clock time. The cache is keyed on package-lock.json's hash, so it's automatically invalidated when dependencies actually change — you get speed without stale installs.
